**背景**：手写 `mocks` 繁琐；已有 OpenAPI/Swagger 文档的项目应能直接生成。

**验收**
- `httpeek mock --from-openapi spec.json --port 8080` 读取 `paths` 与 `responses`，为每个 path + method 生成一条 mock（用文档里的 example 或按 schema 生成占位值）。
- 生成的路由可直接被 `httpeek get` 命中。
- 在 README「集合文件格式」里补充一小节。

**提示**：OpenAPI 多为 JSON（少数 YAML 需说明不支持）；从 `paths[path][method].responses[code].content` 提取示例。放在新文件 `openapi.py`。

**约束**：本项目零第三方依赖（只用 Python 标准库）。
title: [Feature] 从 OpenAPI 自动生成 mocks

body:
## Context

Postman published an experiment on November 12, 2026 showing API simulations shared across coding agent sessions. One agent session generated Inventory and Payments mocks from OpenAPI specs, composed a baseline simulation plus three failure variants (409 out of stock, 402 payment declined, 8 second payment timeout), and published all four to a workspace. A second, fresh agent session listed the simulations with the Postman CLI, pulled one, ran it locally on a single port, and built a checkout service against it. The timeout variant surfaced a real unknown-outcome bug that code reading had missed.

Source: https://blog.postman.com/sharing-api-simulations-across-coding-agent-sessions/

## Gap

MockForge already has scenarios, failure simulation, and an MCP control surface (open issue 1489), plus a simulation handoff context file (filed issue 1549). What it does not have is a publishable, discoverable simulation bundle: a versioned artifact a service owner maintains, including failure variants, that another developer or a fresh agent session can list, pull, and run with one command instead of rediscovering dependency behavior from source.

## Proposed scope

- Export a simulation bundle from a MockForge project: mocks, routes, scenario state, and named failure variants, with the source spec version recorded.
- A CLI flow to list available bundles, pull one, and run it locally on one port with path routing across services, comparable to postman simulation list and postman simulation run.
- A bundle manifest an agent session can read before running: services covered, variants included, ports and routes, and how to switch variants.
- Bundles stay git-friendly files in a repo or workspace folder for v1. No hosted registry is required for this issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- A bundle exported from one project runs in a clean directory with a single command and serves the baseline behavior.
- Switching to a named failure variant changes behavior without editing the bundle by hand.
- An agent session with no prior cont what a bundle covers from its manifest alone.
- Docs describe the bundle format and the list, pull, and run flow.
title: Publishable simulation bundles: share owner-maintained mocks and failure variants that agent sessions can list, pull, and run

body:
## Problem

The connector emulator (`@kbn/connector-emulate`) builds its mocks from OpenAPI, and converts the other formats vendors publish into OpenAPI first (Swagger 2 with `convertSwagger2`, Google Discovery documents with `convertDiscovery`). A connector whose vendor publishes none of these is exempt in `vendor_api_exemptions.json`: it gets no contract test, no mock and no drift detection.

Some of those vendors do publish a machine-readable description of their API, as Markdown rather than OpenAPI: an `llms.txt` index linking one page per endpoint, each written from a fixed template and generated from the vendor's own API description. These pages carry what the emulator needs, such as methods, paths, typed parameters, request bodies, response fields and enums, in a form a parser can read reliably.

## Proposal

A converter from Markdown API references to OpenAPI 3.0 in `@kbn/connector-emulate`, alongside `convertSwagger2` and `convertDiscovery`:

- **A shared core** that turns parsed endpoints into OpenAPI operations and schemas: server and path, parameters by location, request bodies, nested response schemas, and type mapping (`int64`, arrays, enums, defaults, ranges, `required`, `deprecated`, nullable).
- **One parser per vendor template**, since each vendor writes its pages differently. Adding a vendor with a similar reference means adding a parser, not a new pipeline.
- **A way to list the pages** an `llms.txt` index links to, so a source can name the index and the pages or API groups to include.
- What a template can't express (responses given only as examples, `oneOf` variants) is corrected with `overlay.yaml` actions, as for vendor OpenAPI defects, not in the parser.

## Motivating vendors

Two exempt connectors have such a reference today:

| Connector | Reference | Template | What the connector calls |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `.databricks` | [`docs.databricks.com/api/llms.txt`](https://docs.databricks.com/api/llms.txt), ~1,500 pages, e.g. [`jobs/v2/run-now.md`](https://docs.databricks.com/api/jobs/v2/run-now.md) and the object page [`uc-schemas/v1/schema/object.md`](https://docs.databricks.com/api/uc-schemas/v1/schema/object.md) | Method and path line; path, query and body parameters as bullet lists with type and required/optional/deprecated; separate object pages with attribute types, nesting and "Possible values" enums | Jobs runs, clusters, SQL warehouses and SQL alerts; some actions use the managed SQL MCP server (`/api/2.0/mcp/sql`) and would be `unmatched`, as for GitHub and PagerDuty |
| `.brave-search` | [`api-dashboard.search.brave.com/llms.txt`](https://api-dashboard.search.brave.com/llms.txt), one page per endpoint, e.g. [`api-reference/web/search/get/index.html.md`](https://api-dashboard.search.brave.com/api-reference/web/search/get/index.html.md) | Method and path as code spans with a `Base URL` line; parameter, header and authorization tables (Name, Location, Type, Required, Constraints, Description) with enums and defaults in Constraints; a flat response table whose field names encode nesting (`query.language.main`, `results[].thumbnail.src`) | `webSearch`: `GET https://api.search.brave.com/res/v1/web/search` (the reference documents `/v1/web/search`; check how it resolves against the base URL) |

## Acceptance

- The pages both connectors call convert to OpenAPI documents that load in the emulator and serve the connectors' calls, e.g. Databricks' `POST /api/2.2/jobs/run-now` and Brave's web search, with their parameters, request bodies and response schemas.
- Tests for the shared core and for each parser, covering parameters by location, nested response fields, enums and defaults, and Databricks' deprecated fields and object pages.

The source format in `manifest.json` (handled by `loadVendorSpec`, `--inspect` and recording), recording `.databricks` and `.brave-search`, removing their exemptions and drift detection of these sources are #299487.

Part of #295699; follows #295688.
title: [Connector validation][Emulator] Convert Markdown API references to OpenAPI
